applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along OHE line, southwest cluster and southeast cluster planting areas
findings.comment: Mitigation trees including Cedar Elm, Live Oak, and Mexican Redbud are proposed 0 to 2.3 feet from the overhead electric distribution line conductor, far below the required 15-foot minimum clearance for non-utility-compatible trees. These species are not listed as utility-compatible in ECM Appendix F and must be relocated to provide minimum 15-foot lateral clearance from the outside conductor, or replaced with utility-compatible species.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along OHE line near southwest and southeast clusters
findings.comment: Cedar Elm (proposed 10 specimens at 100 gal., 16' minimum height) and Live Oak (proposed 2 specimens at 100 gal., 16' minimum height) have mature heights of 40-60 feet and 40-50+ feet respectively, meeting the 40+ foot threshold for large trees. These large trees are proposed 0 to 2.3 feet from the overhead electric distribution conductor, violating the required 25-foot minimum clearance for large trees. Trees must be relocated to provide 25-foot lateral clearance from the outside conductor.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where utility poles are located on OHE line
findings.comment: Mitigation trees are proposed 0 to 2.3 feet from the overhead electric line where utility poles are located, violating the 10-foot minimum clearance requirement from utility poles. Trees in southwest and southeast clusters along the southern boundary must be relocated to provide minimum 10-foot lateral clearance from all utility poles on the OHE line.

applicableAreas: Landscape plan in areas near overhead electric distribution line
findings.comment: While the plant schedule on Sheet 35 identifies large trees (Cedar Elm and Live Oak with 40+ foot mature heights), these large tree species are not clearly differentiated or marked on the landscape plan drawing (Sheet 31) to enable verification of their locations relative to the overhead electric distribution line. Clear marking or legend indicating which tree symbols represent large trees is required to verify compliance with 25-foot clearance requirements.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where mitigation trees are proposed within prohibited clearance zones (0-2.3 feet from OHE conductor)
findings.comment: Mitigation trees (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud) are proposed 0 to 2.3 feet from the overhead electric distribution conductor, placing them within prohibited clearance zones (less than 15 feet for non-utility-compatible trees, less than 25 feet for large trees). No documented written approval from Austin Energy is provided on the submitted plans authorizing this clearance variance. Obtain explicit written approval from Austin Energy, or relocate trees to comply with minimum clearance distances.

applicableAreas: Areas with proposed pad-mounted electric equipment
findings.comment: Pad-mounted electric equipment locations are not shown on the landscape plan (Sheet 31) in relation to the proposed trees. While the electrical design plan (Sheet 21) may show equipment locations, these are not coordinated or referenced on the landscape plan, preventing verification of whether any proposed trees are within the required 10-foot clearance from pad-mounted equipment or access doors.

applicableAreas: Areas with proposed underground electric equipment
findings.comment: Underground electric equipment (pull boxes, transformers, vaults) locations are not shown on the landscape plan in relation to proposed trees. The electrical design plan (Sheet 21) details underground infrastructure, but these locations are not cross-referenced on the landscape plan, preventing verification that proposed trees comply with the 5-foot minimum clearance from underground electric equipment.

applicableAreas: Areas with trees proposed within 20 feet of underground electric equipment
findings.comment: Required root barrier specifications (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from underground electric equipment) are not shown on the landscape plan or in the landscape details/notes. Without coordination between underground equipment locations and proposed tree locations, and without visible root barrier specifications on the submitted plans, compliance with root barrier requirements cannot be verified.
